claim.why_it_matters: A section heading demoted to plain text drops it from the document structure, so heading-based navigation and section slicing miss the clause boundary.
claim.note: Printed as a section heading (sibling of 3.8.3 Syntax Rules, which the markdown renders as '### 3.8.3 Syntax Rules'); the markdown demotes it to a plain paragraph with no heading marker.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page 600 (folio XIII-18, Report Writer - PAGE) shows '3.8.4 General Rules' as a numbered subsection heading on its own line, the same style as its siblings. In specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md the Report Writer PAGE clause renders its siblings as headings ('### 3.8.1 Function' line 22580, '### 3.8.2 General Format' 22584, '### 3.8.3 Syntax Rules' 22596, '### 3.8.5 Page Regions' 22678), but line 22640 is the plain paragraph '3.8.4 General Rules' with no heading marker. The text is present and correct; only the heading level is lost, so this is a genuine structural (not normative) discrepancy, accurately described.
